title: Usage-tier decoupling and timebound overage fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures requirements and acceptance criteria for decoupling usage tiers from strict hard caps and introducing a timebound overage fallback mechanism that lets customers exceed plan quotas for short, auditable windows while ensuring deterministic billing and reconciliation. The feature aims to reduce operational incidents caused by abrupt hard throttles, improve customer experience during spikes, and preserve predictable invoicing for finance teams.

Background and motivation:
- Multiple customer escalations in Q4 2024 highlighted pain when quota hard-stops broke production flows (chatbots, search rerankers) during transient traffic spikes.
- Current behavior: quota exceeded -> immediate 429/403 depending on route, leading to user-visible errors and manual support credits.
- Goal: provide a controlled, observable fallback path that permits short bursts above quota (timebound overage windows), attaches clear billing items, and supports per-route/ model attribution so we can triage cost and quality regressions.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce customer incidents attributable to quota hard-stops by 60% for customers on priority plans in first 90 days.
- All overage events produce line-item billing with SKU, units consumed, and timestamp; invoices to match usage ledger within one billing cycle with <0.1% reconciliation delta.
- Support per-route rate limits and entitlements mapping so platform can report which API routes caused overage.

Scope (in):
- Policy engine changes to allow configurable timebound overage windows per plan (window length 1-60 minutes).
- Metering improvements to tag overage consumption and emit billing events immediately to the billing ledger.
- API/Console controls for admins to set plan-level overage policies: allow/deny, window length, max overage multiplier.
- Acceptance criteria automation and QA test plans.

Scope (out):
- Billing UI redesign (invoice viewer improvements) — separate ticket.
- Complex cross-tenant credit pooling — separate initiative.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Eng: Marco Li (assignee), ENG-21054 runtime metering workstream
- Billing/Finance: Priya Menon (review)
- Solutions/SE: Carlos Ortega (customer rollout)
- Legal/Compliance: for enterprise contract text updates (consultation only)

High-level design notes:
- Each plan gets an overage_policy object (in config store) with fields: allow_overage (bool), window_minutes (int), max_multiplier (float), per_route (bool).
- When a request would exceed a quota, the policy engine checks remaining window allowance and either: 1) permit the request and tag it as overage, 2) reject with standard quota error.
- Metering: overage-tagged tokens/units are emitted to a fast path billing topic (Kafka) with metadata: customer_id, plan_id, route, model, token_count, timestamp, window_id. Billing ledger consumer must be able to idempotently ingest these events.
- Automatic drafting: when overage occurs, the customer gets a diagnostic event visible in the Console timeline and an email (configurable).

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We prefer short windows (1-15 minutes) for most plans to avoid long tails on unbounded overage exposure; enterprise plans can go up to 60 minutes.
- Chose tagging+fast-path events (vs immediate invoice generation) to minimize latency impacts on runtime and keep invoicing in batch. Finance validated ledger ingestion SLA.
- If overage volume exceeds 'max_multiplier' (e.g., 3x quota) during a window, throttle to preserve fairness. This prevents runaway cost exposure.

Acceptance criteria (product + billing):
1) Policy behavior:
  - Given a plan with allow_overage=true and window_minutes=10 and max_multiplier=2.0, when a customer consumes 1.8x their quota within the 10-minute window, requests are allowed and tagged as overage.
  - When customer tries to consume >2.0x within same window, requests are throttled with a standardized throttling error code and human-readable message pointing to Console.

2) Metering and billing events:
  - Every overage-tagged unit generates a billing event to billing-topic within 5s of request completion (95th percentile).
  - Billing events include customer_id, plan_id, route, model, raw_units, window_id, event_id (UUID), and a versioned schema identifier.
  - Billing consumer guarantees idempotency: if the same event_id is submitted twice, only one ledger entry is created. Ledger records must store event_id and ingestion timestamp.

3) Invoice and reconciliation:
  - Overage line items are present on the next invoice as: SKU: OVERAGE-{plan_id}-{route}, quantity = summed raw_units, unit_price = plan.overage_price_per_unit.
  - Finance reconciliation job (batch) matches consumption events to invoice lines with >= 99.9% match rate. Any mismatch >0.1% triggers automated alert to billing ops.

4) Console visibility and customer notifications:
  - Console shows real-time timeline entries for overage windows with aggregated units and estimated cost (within 5% accuracy).
  - Customers receive optional email notifications when cumulative overage reaches thresholds (10%, 50%, 100% of monthly commit).

5) Observability and SLOs:
  - Over-age-metering pipeline end-to-end P95 latency < 10s for event ingestion into ledger (measured in staging).
  - Alerts created for (a) ingestion failure rate >0.5% in 5m window, (b) mismatch rate >0.1% between ledger and invoicing job.

6) Tests and QA:
  - Integration test simulating a spike: consume 2.5x quota in 5m - expect allow for first 2.0x and throttle thereafter; billing events recorded for 2.0x units only.
  - Load test with 100 concurrent customers each producing overage windows; billing consumer must sustain target throughput without dropping events.
  - Regression tests ensuring legacy plans with allow_overage=false remain unchanged (hard-stop behavior).

Implementation notes / deliverables:
- ENG: add overage_policy config, policy engine checks, tagging at runtime path, billing_topic producer, schema registry entries. (ENG-21054 to implement runtime).
- Billing: schema review and ledger ingestion pipeline consumer update. Provide test harness/ mock events.
- Console: timeline UI tile and notification toggle. Small PRD and mockups located in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PR/pages/654321234/Timebound+Overage+Fallbacks (internal).
- Docs: Customer-facing KB article draft in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-overage-kb (link for SEs).

Progress updates (journal):
- 2025-02-18: Drafted PRD and initial ACs. Shared with Finance and Eng. (Aisha)
- 2025-02-21: Architecture sync: agreed on fast-path billing topic and idempotent event IDs. (Marco, Priya)
- 2025-02-27: Eng spike completed to measure cost of tagging runtime: P95 additional latency ~3ms. Decided acceptable. (Marco)
- 2025-03-03: Finance completed schema review with minor field changes (added window_id). (Priya)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How should refunds/credits be handled if a reconciliation later finds duplicate events? Proposal: billing ops to apply manual credit workflow and we add a follow-up automation to auto-reverse duplicates detected within 7 days. (Action: billing to design).
- Enterprise contract language: need legal to sign off on explicit overage terms. (Action: Legal outreach by 2025-03-10).
- Rollout gating: Should we default to opt-in for all customers for first 6 weeks? Proposed: enable for low-risk customers automatically, require consent for high-risk/offshore regions. (Action: PM to finalize).

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal + 5 low-risk customers (2 weeks) -> monitor incidents and reconciliation deltas.
- Beta: select customer cohort + SE-assisted onboarding (4 weeks).
- GA: enable by plan configuration for new and existing plans; default policy = allow_overage=false unless customer opts in.
